properties.trigger: any competition tagged basketball; a basketball game, box score, roster, rotation, trade, draft, standings, play-in, series or fantasy basketball lineup; a basketball position, stat key or stage not yet in this world
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, venue, stat_line

data.short_description: Basketball at every level: top-flight and women's pro leagues, the continental club competition and national-team play, college, rec leagues and pickup. Positions and combos, full box-score vocabulary with derived shooting and advanced rates, pro and international and college tiebreakers, play-in and best-of series, two-way contracts and affiliate assignments, the draft and lottery, trades as text, officials, and the sport-specific half of fantasy basketball (slots, nine categories, daily lineups).

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport: basketball, at every level: a national top-flight pro league, a women's pro league, the continental club competition and national-team play under the international federation's rules, college, high school, adult rec leagues and pickup runs. Code basketball. Human name: basketball. One pack covers all of them; the level-specific differences are in the Recreational and Professional chunks, and each competition's House rules chunk picks its rule set.
A match is a game. Its parts are periods: four quarters in most pro leagues (12 minutes in the top men's league, 10 under international rules and in most women's and pro leagues elsewhere) or two 20-minute halves in men's college basketball and most rec leagues (women's college plays four 10-minute quarters). Overtime periods are 5 minutes (rec leagues often 2 or 3, or first-to-N points) and repeat until someone leads, so a basketball game never ends level: result is home_win or away_win, never draw. result tie is legal only when a rec league's House rules say a game can end tied at the time limit. decided_by: regulation, overtime (score_display says how many: "131-127 2OT"), awarded (a forfeit's awarded score), run_rule (rec leagues that stop at a margin), time_limit (rec running-clock games called at the horn with no overtime), called_game (an abandoned game the league counts as final at the stoppage), walkover.
The single score number is points. home_score/away_score are the final points. Period scores are not on the event and event.periods stays empty in this sport: they are keys on each team's match stat_line (points_q1.. or points_h1/points_h2, points_ot1..).
Format differences the AI must not blur: three-point line (7.24 m at the top of the arc in the top men's league, 6.75 m under international rules and in college men's and women's play since 2019/2021), personal fouls to disqualification (6 in the top men's league and the women's pro league; 5 under international rules, in college and in nearly every rec league), shot clock (24 s pro and international, 30 s college, often none in rec), team-foul bonus (pro: 5th team foul per quarter; international: 5th; college: 7th in a half or 5th in a quarter for women), timeouts, jump ball vs possession arrow (pro leagues jump; international and college use the arrow), and overtime length. The pack stores the same stat keys everywhere; these differences change how fouls and periods are read, not the vocabulary. Write a competition's rule set in its House rules chunk (competition.match_format stays empty; basketball has one match format and these are rule differences): periods, period length, running or stopped clock, fouls to disqualification, shot clock, overtime rule, mercy rule, time limit.
Default competition for a pro league: level pro, format league_playoffs, scoring_system win_loss, governing_body the league's office, rounds_total left empty (an 82-game season has no rounds; put the game count in ruleset_notes). A rec league: level recreational, format round_robin or league_playoffs, scoring_system win_loss (or 2-1-0 where the league keeps a points table, common under international-style rules: 2 for a win, 1 for a loss, 0 for a forfeit). A college conference: level college. A national-team tournament: level international, format group_knockout. A fantasy league: level fantasy, see the Fantasy chunk.
Season labels: a pro season spans two calendar years and is labelled "2026-27"; the season tag is <competition-slug-fragment>-2026-27. A rec league with several seasons a year labels them "Winter 2026", "Spring 2026". Every entity in this sport carries the tag basketball.
Home and away: the designated home team is home even at a neutral or overseas arena (HELD_AT the real arena, neutral_site false). A tournament game on a neutral floor is neutral_site true with neutral_first/neutral_second.
A generic league shape for the 30-team, two-conference, six-division shape ships as league-shapes/pro-league-30-two-conferences.json; onboarding renames its placeholder teams and, when it creates the first season, writes each team's COMPETES_IN conference and group from the team's conference-* and division-* tags.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes on PLAYS_FOR.position (and PLAYED_IN.position when the player played elsewhere on the night). Modern rosters list combos; store the combo the team lists, and put the components in secondary_positions when it helps a fantasy eligibility check.
PG   point guard: the primary ball handler
SG   shooting guard
SF   small forward
PF   power forward
C    center
G    guard (PG/SG combo, as modern rosters list it)
F    forward (SF/PF combo)
G-F  guard-forward (wing, SG/SF)
F-C  forward-center (big, PF/C)
F-G  forward-guard: use G-F instead; this spelling is only for matching imports
UTIL utility: fantasy slot only, not a roster position
Numbering: 1 through 5 (point guard through center) is how coaches talk; map 1=PG, 2=SG, 3=SF, 4=PF, 5=C when the owner uses numbers. Never store a number as a position.
Roles on PLAYS_FOR.role: starter (the five who start), rotation (plays regular minutes off the bench), bench (dressed, sparse minutes), reserve (on the roster but not dressing: affiliate assignment, two-way player not with the senior team, a formal inactive list), captain, injured_reserve (only in a league whose House rules name an injured list that takes the player off the roster count; the 30-team pro league has none, so there a player who is out is availability only). Which list the player counts against is roster_list (Roster rules). Rotation order, when the owner wants it, is depth_order on PLAYS_FOR (1-5 the starters, 6 the sixth man, 7-10 the rest of the rotation); update it in place as the rotation changes.
Handedness on person: right, left, both (shooting hand). Height and weight are optional, adult pros only, and never asked for.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
stage values on events and seasons: preseason, regular_season, cup_group (an in-season cup's group games, which also count as regular-season games: see below), cup_knockout (cup quarterfinals and semifinals, also count), cup_final (does not count in the standings), all_star (exhibition, never counts), play_in, first_round, conference_semifinal, conference_final, final (the championship series), group_stage, round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, third_place, playoff (a rec league's generic post-season), consolation, friendly, exhibition, tournament (a weekend tournament inside a rec season), offseason (season.stage only).
round: optional in a pro regular season (there are no matchdays; leave it empty or write "Game 23 of 82" if the owner counts). Rec leagues: "Week 7". Cups and continental competitions: "Round 12", "Group A". Play-in: "7-8 game", "9-10 game", "8 seed game". Series games: "Game 1" to "Game 7". Draft: "Round 1", "Round 2".
Best-of series: one parent event (event_type match, stage from the list above, named "<Lower seed> vs <Higher seed> — <stage> <season>", score_display "4-3", result from the higher seed's point of view as first-named, neutral_site false, date_* of Game 1, end_date of the last game) PART_OF the season, with COMPETED_IN from both teams; one child event per game (round "Game N", home/away as played) PART_OF the parent. Home-court pattern in a best-of-7 is 2-2-1-1-1: the higher seed hosts Games 1, 2, 5 and 7. A best-of-5 first round (some leagues) is 2-2-1. Team season records never include series games; a series line (series_wins, series_losses) is a season-line key for the playoffs only.
Play-in: in a 30-team league, seeds 7-10 in each conference play after the regular season: 7 v 8 (winner is the 7 seed), 9 v 10 (loser is out), then the 7-8 loser hosts the 9-10 winner for the 8 seed. These are single games, stage play_in, PART_OF the season. Set COMPETES_IN seed when the play-in resolves, status eliminated for the two teams that drop out.
In-season cup: group games (stage cup_group) and knockout games before the final (cup_knockout) are regular-season games for the standings and are PART_OF both the season and a parent event for the cup (event_type match, stage tournament, named "<Cup> <season>", PART_OF the season); the final (cup_final) is PART_OF the cup parent only and counts for nothing but the trophy (WON title "Cup Champion"). Tag every cup game in-season-cup; the two PART_OF edges are what make a cup game count for both the table and the cup.
Continental club competition: a double round-robin regular season (stage regular_season, round "Round N"), then play_in, then best-of-5 playoffs (stage quarterfinal, series as above), then a single-site final four (semifinal, third_place, final; neutral_site true).
National-team tournaments: group_stage with round "Group C", then round_of_16, quarterfinal, semifinal, third_place, final.
decided_by values: regulation, overtime, awarded, run_rule, time_limit, called_game, walkover.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All keys lowercase snake_case, starting with a letter, values numbers; minutes may be decimal (34.5), plus_minus may be negative, everything else integers. null = not recorded (the usual state in a rec book). Rate stats marked DERIVED are never stored: the AI computes them from the components when asked, says how many games the components cover, and states the formula when it matters. Store a typed-in published rate only on a season line whose components are null, source official or owner.

PLAYER — playing time and scoring
minutes          minutes played (stored here, not on PLAYED_IN.minutes, so leaders can be filtered)
pts              points scored
fgm              field goals made (two- and three-pointers together)
fga              field goals attempted
fg3m             three-point field goals made
fg3a             three-point field goals attempted
ftm              free throws made
fta              free throws attempted
fg2m             DERIVED = fgm - fg3m
fg2a             DERIVED = fga - fg3a
fg_pct           DERIVED = fgm / fga * 100
fg3_pct          DERIVED = fg3m / fg3a * 100
ft_pct           DERIVED = ftm / fta * 100
efg_pct          DERIVED effective field goal % = (fgm + 0.5 * fg3m) / fga * 100
ts_pct           DERIVED true shooting % = pts / (2 * (fga + 0.44 * fta)) * 100
ppg              DERIVED = pts / games_played (season or career lines)
and_ones         fouled on a made basket (optional)
points_in_paint  player's points in the paint (optional)
fast_break_points player's fast-break points (optional)
second_chance_points (optional)

PLAYER — rebounding, playmaking, defence, errors
oreb             offensive rebounds
dreb             defensive rebounds
reb              total rebounds; store it when the book gives only a total, otherwise DERIVED = oreb + dreb (never store all three unless the book does)
ast              assists
stl              steals
blk              blocks
tov              turnovers
pf               personal fouls (all fouls charged to the player)
tf               technical fouls
flagrant_fouls   flagrant (international: unsportsmanlike) fouls
disqualifications 1 when fouled out or ejected in this game
ejections        1 when ejected
plus_minus       team margin while on the floor
double_doubles   count (season/career lines; a match line has 1 or 0)
triple_doubles   count
blocks_against   times the player's shot was blocked (optional)
fouls_drawn      personal fouls drawn (optional)
ast_tov_ratio    DERIVED = ast / tov
rpg, apg, spg, bpg, mpg   DERIVED per-game = total / games_played
starts           games started (season/career lines; match lines use PLAYED_IN.started)
games_played     is a stat_line property, not a key

PLAYER — advanced (optional, usually imported; store only when a source publishes them)
usage_pct        imported; DERIVED version = 100 * ((fga + 0.44 * fta + tov) * (team_minutes / 5)) / (minutes * (team_fga + 0.44 * team_fta + team_tov)) needs the team line
per              player efficiency rating, imported only (the full formula needs league pace and averages this world cannot compute honestly)
game_score       DERIVED (the common box-score summary) = pts + 0.4*fgm - 0.7*fga - 0.4*(fta - ftm) + 0.7*oreb + 0.3*dreb + stl + 0.7*ast + 0.7*blk - 0.4*pf - tov
oreb_pct, dreb_pct, ast_pct, stl_pct, blk_pct, tov_pct   imported only
off_rating, def_rating, net_rating   imported only for players (team versions below are derivable)
bpm, vorp, win_shares and other published all-in-one metrics   imported only, under the source's own lowercase key; name the source in source_url
efficiency       DERIVED (the simple EFF used by the international federation and the continental competition) = (pts + reb + ast + stl + blk) - ((fga - fgm) + (fta - ftm) + tov)
pir              DERIVED performance index rating (continental competition) = (pts + reb + ast + stl + blk + fouls_drawn) - ((fga - fgm) + (fta - ftm) + tov + blocks_against + pf)

TEAM — per game (team match line; the final score stays on the event)
points_q1 .. points_q4, points_ot1 .. points_ot4   period scores for quarters formats
points_h1, points_h2                                 period scores for halves formats
fgm fga fg3m fg3a ftm fta oreb dreb reb ast stl blk tov pf tf   team totals, same meaning as the player keys
team_rebounds    rebounds credited to the team, not a player
points_in_paint, fast_break_points, second_chance_points, points_off_turnovers, bench_points
biggest_lead     largest lead at any point
lead_changes, times_tied
timeouts_left    timeouts remaining at the end
possessions      stored only when a source gives it; DERIVED estimate = fga - oreb + tov + 0.44 * fta (per team; average the two teams' estimates for the game)
pace             DERIVED = 48 * possessions / (minutes_total / 5), where minutes_total is 240 for a regulation 48-minute game (40-minute games use 40 and 200); say which
off_rating       DERIVED = points scored / possessions * 100
def_rating       DERIVED = points allowed / possessions * 100
net_rating       DERIVED = off_rating - def_rating
fg_pct, fg3_pct, ft_pct, efg_pct, ts_pct   DERIVED as for players
tov_pct          DERIVED = tov / possessions * 100
oreb_pct         DERIVED = oreb / (oreb + opponent dreb) * 100 (needs the opponent's team line)
ft_rate          DERIVED = fta / fga

TEAM — season (standings keys are in the Standings chunk)
points_for       total points scored (regular season)
points_against   total points allowed
margin           DERIVED = (points_for - points_against) / games_played
Fantasy keys (fantasy_points, projected_points, games_counted, games_scheduled and the category totals) are in the Fantasy chunk and live only on lines RECORDED_IN fantasy events.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Keys on a team season line (scope season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the season, source derived when the AI built it): wins, losses, ties (rec leagues that allow them, else 0), points_for, points_against, home_wins, home_losses, away_wins, away_losses, division_wins, division_losses, conference_wins, conference_losses, forfeit_wins, forfeit_losses, streak (positive = current winning streak in games, negative = losing streak), last_10_wins, last_10_losses, standings_points (points-table leagues: 2 per win, 1 per loss, 0 per forfeit under international-style rules, or whatever House rules say), series_wins, series_losses (playoffs only, never in the table). games_played is the stat_line property. Count only completed or forfeited events whose stage is regular_season, cup_group or cup_knockout; preseason, all_star, cup_final, play_in and playoff games never enter the table.
Columns: Team, W, L, PCT, GB, Conf, Div, Home, Away, L10, Streak, PF, PA, Diff. For points-table leagues: Team, P, W, L, Pts, PF, PA, Diff. win_pct DERIVED = wins / (wins + losses) (ties count half a win where they exist). GB = ((leader wins - team wins) + (team losses - leader losses)) / 2. Group by conference, then show divisions only if the owner asks (division standing matters for one tiebreaker, not for seeding).
Conference and division come from COMPETES_IN: conference holds the conference ("Conference A") and group holds the division alone ("North"), each spelled exactly as the competition's House rules spell them; a single-table league leaves conference empty. A division game is one where both teams' conference and group match; a conference game is one where only conference matches.
Tiebreakers, 30-team pro league (two teams): 1. head-to-head record; 2. division winner (only if one of them won its division); 3. division record (same division only); 4. conference record; 5. record against playoff-eligible teams in own conference (teams finishing 1-10 after the regular season); 6. record against playoff-eligible teams in the other conference; 7. point differential (points_for - points_against). Three or more tied: 1. division winner; 2. combined head-to-head record among the tied teams; 3. division record (same division only); 4. conference record; 5. record against playoff-eligible teams in own conference; 6. point differential. Once a multi-team tie reduces to two, restart with the two-team order. Division winners are not guaranteed a top-4 seed; seeding 1-15 in each conference is by record with these tiebreakers, 1-6 go straight to the playoffs, 7-10 to the play-in, 11-15 are out.
Women's pro league: single table (no conferences for seeding in recent formats; check House rules), tiebreakers head-to-head, then point differential against the tied teams, then overall point differential.
International-style points table (continental competition, national federations, many rec leagues): standings_points first (2-1-0); ties on points broken by 1. head-to-head record among the tied teams; 2. point difference in games among the tied teams; 3. points scored in games among the tied teams; 4. overall point difference; 5. overall points scored; 6. draw of lots (report "draw of lots" and leave the order as the owner says). Some competitions use overall point difference before head-to-head: House rules decide.
College conference: conference record first (conference_wins/losses, excluding non-conference games), then head-to-head, then record against the top-seeded common opponent descending, then a published rating system or coin toss. Most conference tournaments seed by this order; the national tournament is a separate knockout competition with seeds the committee assigns (COMPETES_IN seed 1-16 per region, group the region name).
Rec league default: win_pct, head-to-head, point differential (capped per game if House rules say, commonly +/-20), points against, coin toss. Forfeit wins count as wins; the forfeit score (default 20-0, House rules decide) enters points_for/against only if the league says so.
Always name the tiebreaker that split any tied teams, say how many games the lines cover, and when the owner has not logged every game in the league, give only their own team's record and splits and say the table is partial. Record against playoff-eligible teams cannot be computed until the regular season is over or every team's record is on file; say so instead of estimating.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Pro, 30-team league: 15 standard contracts plus up to 3 two-way contracts (18 under contract); 13 active for a game (12 if the roster is at 14 or fewer), the rest inactive. Record an inactive with PLAYED_IN played false, no reason. Starting five: PLAYED_IN started true for exactly five players per team per game. Sanity check on a full box score: team minutes sum to 240 for a regulation 48-minute game (200 for 40-minute formats) plus 25 per overtime (5 per 5-minute period); flag a box score that is off by more than a minute instead of saving it silently. Five players on the floor; substitutions are unlimited and are not recorded individually (entered_at is optional).
Lists and roles: roster_list on the senior-team edge says which count the player is in, in this pack's vocabulary: standard (one of the 15 standard contracts), two_way (one of the 3 two-way slots), hardship (a contract granted above the 15 under a hardship exception), affiliate (on the affiliate edge only). role says what they are to the team (starter, rotation, bench, reserve, captain). Write roster_list for every pro edge and leave it empty for college and rec; write role whenever the owner knows it. Game-day active or inactive is a per-game fact (PLAYED_IN played false), never a roster_list value. Every change of list (two-way conversion, hardship signing, assignment, recall) is a roster_move event (INVOLVED_IN the player role subject with detail naming the move, the team role to_team) that updates roster_list, role or availability on the edge.
Two-way contracts: arrangement two_way and roster_list two_way on the PLAYS_FOR edge to the senior team. A two-way player is limited to 50 active senior-team games per season (fewer if signed late) and is ineligible for the playoffs; the AI counts games_played on their senior-team season line and warns at 45. Development-league assignment: a second open PLAYS_FOR to the affiliate team (team_type franchise, PART_OF the senior team) with arrangement loan, acquired_via loan, started the assignment date; the senior edge's role becomes reserve. Recall: end the affiliate edge, restore the role. Players on a standard contract can be assigned the same way (no limit) and so can draft-and-stash rights holders who sign an affiliate contract (then the senior team has no edge; a lore chunk Draft rights on the person names the team holding the rights). Hardship exceptions (a 16th or 17th player signed when four or more are out): arrangement contract, roster_list hardship, fee text "hardship, 10-day", nothing about why the others are out.
Availability: the daily report maps to availability only. Out = unavailable, Doubtful = doubtful, Questionable = doubtful, Probable = available, Available = available. The reason column (body part, illness, rest, personal reasons, return to competition reconditioning, league suspension) is never stored except a suspension, which is availability suspended with availability_until the date it lapses and the league's stated length and policy name in lore on the person. A DNP is PLAYED_IN played false. The owner typing "out with a knee" gets the availability change and one line saying this world keeps no health details.
Contracts and the cap: fee is text on PLAYS_FOR ("4y/$120M", "two-way", "10-day", "rookie scale 1.07", "min, 1y") and in INVOLVED_IN detail on the signing event. Extensions: a signing event with detail starting "extension:", the edge stays open with fee updated. Options, guarantees, trade kickers, aprons, exceptions used (mid-level, bi-annual, trade exception) are lore on the person or the trade event, owner's wording. The world does no cap arithmetic.
Trades: one trade event, INVOLVED_IN each team role other with detail "sends: ... / receives: ...", each player traded_away or acquired with detail the destination team. Salary matching ("matched within 125%", "absorbed into the room exception") and picks ("2027 R1 (own, top-4 protected)", "2028 R2 swap rights") are text in detail and a lore chunk Trade notes. Three- and four-team trades are one event. A trade voided by the league is status rejected with "voided by the league" in lore and no reason. Confirm the plan first when a trade touches more than three players. The trade deadline is a date in the Season calendar; a trade logged after it is a flag to ask, not a refusal.
Draft: one event per draft (event_type draft, "Draft 2026", end_date if two days), two rounds of 30 (fewer when teams forfeit picks), INVOLVED_IN person role drafted with detail "Round 1, Pick 7 (7 overall)" and team role drafting_team; a pick traded on the night is a separate trade event. The lottery is an event with event_type other ("Draft Lottery 2026"), INVOLVED_IN each of the 14 non-playoff teams role other with detail "odds 14.0%, won pick 1". Draft rights without a contract: no PLAYS_FOR until signed, lore chunk Draft rights. Rookie signing: signing event, acquired_via draft, fee "rookie scale <pick>". Second-round picks often sign two-way deals: arrangement two_way, roster_list two_way, acquired_via draft. Undrafted free agents: acquired_via free_agent.
Free agency and waivers: signing event with acquired_via free_agent; a release is event release (end the edge, person status free_agent when no other open playing edge); a successful waiver claim is a roster_move with acquired_via waiver on the new edge and the former team as from_team on the event; a lost claim, when the owner wants it recorded, is the same roster_move with status rejected. 10-day contracts: arrangement contract, fee "10-day", ended ten days later unless re-signed (a second 10-day is a second edge; a third must be a rest-of-season deal).
College: 13 scholarship players (men), 15 (women); arrangement scholarship or amateur (walk-on). Transfers between schools are event transfer with detail "portal", no fee; eligibility years are not tracked unless the owner asks (then lore on the person titled Eligibility, sporting facts only).
Rec: see the Recreational chunk: roster minimum to avoid a forfeit (default 4 players at tip, House rules), rolling subs, co-ed on-floor rules, ringers as arrangement substitute ended the same day.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content: OFFICIATED.role values: crew_chief (the lead official of a three-person pro crew), referee (the second official), umpire (the third official; in a two-person rec crew both officials are referee), alternate_official (the standby who replaces an official who cannot continue), replay_official (the replay-centre reviewer on a pro game), scorer (official scorer at the table), timer (game clock), shot_clock_operator, commissioner_rep (league observer at the table, optional), statistician (the table crew member keeping the box score, in college and the continental competition). Record officials only when the owner names them, and never store an official's grade, fine or evaluation.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: (none yet; keys the owner adds go here, one per line, dated)

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What a rec, church, company, school or pickup league changes: two 20-minute halves (sometimes four 8- or 10-minute quarters) with a running clock that stops only in the last minute or two of each half, 5 fouls to disqualification, a shot clock only if the gym has one, 1-5 minutes of overtime or none (then the game ends tied if House rules allow it: result tie), a mercy rule that runs the clock or ends the game at a margin (decided_by run_rule), a hard time limit when the gym closes (decided_by time_limit), a forfeit when a side cannot field 4 (default 20-0 awarded, decided_by awarded, status forfeited), rolling subs at any dead ball, co-ed rules (a required number of each group on the floor, a different ball, sometimes a three-point premium for one group; the pack never adds a gender key: the owner enforces co-ed rules and the AI records them only as House rules text), ringers (a non-rostered player who turns up: PLAYS_FOR with arrangement substitute started and ended on the game date, said so in lore), and a scorebook that often records nothing but points per player.
Sporadic books are the central fact. On logging a game, ask once whether the book has more than points (fouls? rebounds? threes?) and store null for every key nobody counted. Season lines sum only the keys that were recorded and the AI leads every average with its coverage ("over the 9 games with a book"). A season leaderboard in points is honest; one in rebounds is honest only if rebounds were kept every game, otherwise say so. Fouls are the one thing rec books reliably keep beyond points (because of disqualification), so pf is usually fillable.
Pickup runs: a standing run (Saturday mornings at the community gym) is a competition (level recreational, format round_robin, scoring_system win_loss, tag pickup) with one season per year and no team entities. A game is a match event named "Pickup — <venue> — <date> (Game N)" with score_display "Shirts 21-17 Skins" and home_score/away_score for the two sides, result home_win/away_win where home is the first-named side, and PLAYED_IN edges whose for_team is the side label (shirts, skins, white, dark) rather than a team slug. Only the owner's own numbers are usually worth a stat_line (scope match, stats {pts}). Games to a target score (21, 11 by ones and twos, win by two) are decided_by regulation with the target in House rules.
Youth leagues: the base children rules apply in full. Default to the team score and the owner's child's points, not a roster of children's statistics; no per-player leaderboard of minors unless the owner asks for one; first name and last initial; nothing about height, weight or age group beyond the competition's label ("U14"). Coaches and team parents are STAFF_OF with name and role.
Standings in rec leagues are usually kept by the league office; the AI's table is a check, not the record, and it says so when the two disagree. Many leagues run a round-robin then a single-elimination tournament (stage playoff or tournament, seeds on COMPETES_IN): the generic rec-league league shape fits this shape.
Workflow: rule/basketball_game_log handles the post-game routine for any team the owner plays on or follows.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the top level adds. Season: preseason (4-6 exhibitions, stage preseason, never counted), an 82-game regular season from late October to mid-April with an in-season cup in November and December (group games count in the standings; the final does not), an all-star weekend in February (stage all_star), a trade deadline in early February, the play-in in mid-April, four best-of-7 playoff rounds (first_round, conference_semifinal, conference_final, final) from mid-April to mid-June, the draft lottery in May, the draft in late June (two rounds), free agency opening at the start of July, and summer-league exhibitions (stage exhibition). Women's pro league: May to October, a shorter regular season, a mid-season cup, playoffs with a best-of-3 first round then best-of-5 and a best-of-7 final (check House rules each year), and a different roster size (12 maximum, 11 minimum). Continental club competition: October to May, double round-robin, play-in, best-of-5 quarterfinals, final four. Other national leagues and the international federation's calendar vary; House rules decide.
Awards to record as WON edges to the season: Most Valuable Player, Rookie of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, Sixth Man of the Year, Most Improved Player, Coach of the Year, Clutch Player of the Year, Finals MVP (WON to the final series event), Cup MVP, All-League First/Second/Third Team (title "All-League First Team"), All-Defensive teams, All-Rookie teams, All-Star selection (WON to the all_star event). A games-played threshold for eligibility is a count on the season line, not a health fact.
Staff: STAFF_OF roles head_coach, assistant_coach (title "Associate Head Coach", "Player Development Coach"), general_manager (title "President of Basketball Operations"), owner, president, director (title "Director of Scouting"), analyst, scout, trainer (title "Strength and Conditioning Coach"; never what they treat), equipment, other (title "Video Coordinator"). A coaching change: end the edge, open the interim's edge, event other for the firing.
Modern stats the owner may import: usage, offensive/defensive/net rating, pace, plus-minus-based metrics; store them with source import and source_url, never recompute them against the source, and say which numbers are imported when quoting them beside derived ones.
Affiliates: each senior team's development-league affiliate is a team (team_type franchise, PART_OF the senior team, tag development-league) in its own competition (level semi_pro) when the owner tracks assignments; otherwise the assignment is a lore note on the person and the senior edge's role reserve.
A fan logging one team's season uses rule/basketball_game_log: result, box score, story, roster news, standings refresh, next game.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content:
Fantasy leagues in this sport are run by rule/app_fantasy; every workflow (rosters, lineups, waivers, trades, drafts, matchups, standings, imports) lives there, and a fantasy competition carries sport basketball, level fantasy and two APPLIES_TO edges: rule/app_fantasy and this pack. This chunk supplies only the basketball-specific material: slots, eligibility, the daily-lineup convention, categories, scoring tables and roster sizes. The real players are the same person entities as in the real competition; never create a second person for a fantasy roster.
Lineup slots (PLAYS_FOR.slot on the fantasy edge): PG, SG, G, SF, PF, F, C, UTIL, BN, IL (injured list; the platform's name, recorded as a slot and never with a reason), IL+ (some platforms' second list; store as IL). Default lineup: PG SG G SF PF F C UTIL UTIL (9 active) with 3-4 BN and 1-3 IL; many leagues use 10 active with 2 C or 3 UTIL; House rules on the fantasy competition decide. Eligibility: a player fills PG/SG/G/SF/PF/F/C only if that position or a component of their listed combo (G-F covers SG, SF, G, F) appears in position or secondary_positions on their real-team edge; UTIL takes anyone; the AI checks before saving a lineup and asks rather than refusing when the platform lists a position the real roster does not.
Daily lineups. Most basketball leagues set lineups each game day, not each week, so a weekly matchup event cannot hold the lineup in one slot per player. The pack records it this way, as the sport's reading of rule/app_fantasy's lineup snapshot: slot on the fantasy PLAYS_FOR edge is always the lineup right now and is overwritten freely; each weekly matchup event gets one PLAYED_IN edge per rostered player with for_team the fantasy team, started true if the player was in an active slot on at least one game day that week, played true if any of their games counted, and PLAYED_IN.slot only when one slot held all week; the player's weekly fantasy line (scope match, RECORDED_IN the matchup) carries fantasy_points, projected_points, games_counted (game days in an active slot) and games_scheduled (real games that week) so "you left 2 games on the bench" is answerable; the day-by-day grid, if the manager wants it kept, is a lore chunk on the matchup titled Daily lineups, one line per day. Weekly-lineup leagues use the base pattern unchanged with games_counted = games_scheduled. The real box score stays RECORDED_IN the real game; the fantasy line repeats only what the platform scored.
Scoring formats and what goes on the matchup event: H2H points: home_score/away_score are fantasy points, result from them, ties as House rules (most platforms allow result tie). H2H categories (each category is a win, loss or tie; the matchup result is the categories tally): home_score and away_score are categories won, score_display "6-3-0" (won-lost-tied from the home side), result home_win/away_win/tie; the week's nine totals per team are a round-scope team stat_line RECORDED_IN the matchup (the non-score team line rule/stats allows) with the category keys below. H2H most categories: same, but a week is a single win or loss and home_score/away_score are 1/0. Rotisserie: no matchups; each fantasy team has a season line with the category totals and roto_points, ranked per category (N points for first in a 12-team league down to 1), summed; ties in a category split the points.
Category keys on fantasy team lines (round or season scope): fgm, fga, fg_pct (stored here, because the platform's rounding decides the category; DERIVED everywhere else), ftm, fta, ft_pct (stored, same reason), fg3m, pts, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov, plus the optional dd (double-doubles), td (triple-doubles), fg3_pct, ato (assist-to-turnover ratio, stored), pf, oreb, dreb, roto_points, categories_won, categories_lost, categories_tied. The standard nine: fg_pct, ft_pct, fg3m, pts, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov (tov counts low-wins). Eight-cat drops tov; eleven-cat adds dd and oreb or fg3_pct.
Default points scoring (one common platform convention; House rules override): pts 1, reb 1.2, ast 1.5, stl 3, blk 3, tov -1, fg3m 0.5 (some platforms 0; some count fgm 2 / fga -1 / ftm 1 / fta -1 instead of fg3m), dd 0 or bonus, td 0 or bonus. Alternative "DFS-style": pts 1, reb 1.25, ast 1.5, stl 2, blk 2, tov -0.5, fg3m 0.5, dd 1.5, td 3. Store the table in House rules on the fantasy competition and quote it when checking a player's weekly points against their real line.
Roster size defaults: 13 (10 active + 3 BN) with 1-3 IL; 10- or 12-team leagues; snake draft of 13 rounds or auction with a $200 budget; waivers FAAB or rolling priority; weekly acquisition limits (commonly 4-7 moves per week, stored as a House rule and counted from signing events). Keeper leagues: acquired_via keeper. Games-played and minutes caps per position are platform rules recorded in House rules.
Player match lines on the fantasy side use the real stat keys with the same spelling as the Stat keys chunk, source import, so a 9-cat check reads them directly.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content: and-one: fouled while scoring, the basket counts plus a free throw. Apron: a payroll threshold above the cap and tax that restricts roster moves; text only here. Assist-to-turnover ratio: ast / tov. Back-to-back: games on consecutive days; a count the owner can keep in lore. Bonus: team-foul count that sends every subsequent foul to the free-throw line. Box score: the per-player and team line of a game; a match stat_line here. Clutch: last five minutes within five points; a split_label if tracked. DNP: did not play; PLAYED_IN played false. Double-double: 10+ in two of pts, reb, ast, stl, blk. Draft-and-stash: a drafted player who stays abroad; Draft rights lore, no edge. Final four: the single-site semifinals and final of a continental or college tournament. Four-point play: a made three while fouled plus the free throw. Game score: a one-number box-score summary, DERIVED above. Hack-a-player: deliberately fouling a poor free-throw shooter. Hardship: an extra roster spot granted when several players are out; recorded without reasons. Load management: a reason for rest that this world never stores; availability only. Lottery: the weighted draw for the top picks among non-playoff teams. Mercy rule: a running-clock or early-end rule at a margin, rec leagues (decided_by run_rule). Pace: possessions per 48 minutes. Play-in: the post-season mini-tournament for seeds 7-10. Plus-minus: team margin while a player is on the floor. Possession arrow: alternating possession on held balls (international and college). Rotation: the players who get regular minutes, ordered by depth_order. Running clock: the clock does not stop on whistles. Sixth man: the first substitute off the bench. Stretch four: a power forward who shoots threes; a note, not a position. Supermax: a maximum extension for qualifying veterans; text in fee. Ten-day contract: a short pro contract; a PLAYS_FOR edge of ten days. Trade exception: cap room created by a trade; lore. Triple-double: 10+ in three categories. True shooting: points per shooting possession, DERIVED above. Two-way: a contract split between a senior team and its affiliate; arrangement two_way, roster_list two_way. Usage: share of team possessions used while on the floor. UTIL: the any-position fantasy slot. Walkover: an opponent that never showed, in a tournament; decided_by walkover.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Northern-hemisphere top men's pro league (label "2026-27"): training camp late September; preseason early-mid October; regular season tips in the last week of October; in-season cup group games on set November nights with knockouts and a neutral-site final in mid-December; trade deadline on a Thursday in early February; all-star weekend in mid-February; regular season ends in mid-April; play-in the following Tuesday to Friday; playoffs from the Saturday after, first round, conference semifinals, conference finals, final (mid-June); draft lottery in mid-May; draft in the last week of June; free agency opens on 1 July (the moratorium lifts a few days later); summer league in July. Season status: upcoming until the first regular-season game is completed (preseason does not flip it), active to the final, completed when the champion is set; stage moves preseason → regular_season → play_in → first_round ... → final → offseason.
Women's pro league (label "2026"): training camp late April, regular season mid-May to mid-September, mid-season cup in June, an all-star game in July, playoffs late September to mid-October, draft in April, free agency in January-February.
Continental club competition (label "2026-27"): October to April regular season, play-in and quarterfinals in April, final four in late May.
College (label "2026-27"): practice from late September, regular season early November to early March, conference tournaments in the first two weeks of March, national tournament (a separate knockout competition) mid-March to early April, transfer window and draft declarations in April-May.
International: national-team windows in November, February and the summer; continental championships and the world championship in the northern summer (every four years for the world event, with qualifiers in the windows); the quadrennial Games tournament in July-August.
Rec leagues: Winter, Spring, Summer and Fall seasons of 8-12 weeks each under one competition, with a registration deadline, a bye week around holidays and a one- or two-week tournament to close. Pickup runs have a season per calendar year.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Forfeit: status forfeited, decided_by awarded, the awarded score in home_score/away_score as House rules say (rec default 20-0; a pro forfeit, almost unheard of, is 2-0 by rule and goes in score_display "2-0 (forfeit)"), result accordingly, COMPETED_IN results win/loss, forfeit_wins/forfeit_losses on the season lines, why in lore (not enough players at tip, ineligible player, no-show, unpaid fees; never a medical reason). A friendly played after a forfeit is a second event with stage friendly and status completed, never counted. A double forfeit (neither side fields enough) is status forfeited, result no_result, both teams forfeit_losses, scores null.
Abandoned: a game stopped by a floor problem, a gym closure, a fight or a medical emergency (record the stoppage, never the medical detail) is status abandoned, result no_result, score_display the position when play stopped ("41-38, 6:12 2H"), unless House rules say a game is official after a point (common: three quarters or the start of the second half), in which case status completed with the score at the stoppage and decided_by called_game, and a lore chunk Notes saying when play stopped. Pro leagues resume a halted game from the point of stoppage: it stays one event, status suspended until it resumes, date_* of the original day, end_date the day it finished, and a lore note; a game replayed from scratch is a new event with round "Replay" and lore on both pointing at each other.
Postponed: status postponed, keep the event, new date when known, original date in lore; the pro league's "postponed, league rules" needs no reason stored.
Walkover (tournament opponent withdrew before the tip): status forfeited, decided_by walkover, no scores, COMPETED_IN win for the side that advanced, outcome on the withdrawn team's COMPETES_IN set to withdrew.
Protests: a result under protest is status completed with a lore chunk Protest and tag protested; if the league overturns it, update the scores and result, and record the ruling as an event with event_type other and INVOLVED_IN both teams.

properties.trigger: a basketball game just happened; logging a basketball score, box score, points-only book or lineup; a scoring average, shooting percentage or leaderboard; the next game, availability or the playoff picture for the owner's basketball team; loading a basketball schedule
properties.scope: event, stat_line, team, person, season, venue

data.short_description: The post-game routine for a basketball team the owner plays on, coaches or follows, at any level: result, period scores, box score at whatever depth the book was kept, story, roster news, derived season lines, standings refresh and the next game.

lore.title: What this covers
lore.content: The routine for an owner who plays on, coaches or follows one basketball team at any level: the game just played, its box score (full, partial or points-only), the story, roster news, a standings refresh and the next game. Read rule/sport_basketball first for the vocabulary and the competition's House rules chunk for its rule set (periods, fouls, clock, mercy rule, forfeit score). Everything this rule creates carries the tags basketball, game-log and the season tag.

lore.title: Logging a game
lore.content:
1. Find or create the event (rule/recording_a_match): both teams, date, venue (HELD_AT with field "Court 2" when the gym has several), stage, round for rec weeks, series parent for playoff games. Scores on the event, score_display for overtime ("104-101 OT") or a rec tie, decided_by from the pack. COMPETED_IN result on both edges.
2. Ask once per competition how deep the book goes and remember it as a tag on the competition: book-points (points per player only), book-basic (points, fouls, threes, free throws), book-full (a full box score). Do not ask again; change the tag if the owner starts keeping more.
3. Period scores, when given, go on each team's match stat_line (points_q1.. or points_h1/points_h2, points_ot1..). Team totals (fgm, fga, reb, tov, pf...) on the same line. Check the periods sum to the final score and the player points sum to the team points when a full book is given; report a mismatch and ask which is right rather than saving both.
4. Player lines: one match stat_line per player who played, keys from the pack, null for anything not kept; PLAYED_IN edges with for_team, started (five per side when known), played false for a DNP, no reason. Minutes go on the stat_line, not the edge. Fouled out: pf 5 or 6 per the rule set plus disqualifications 1. A ringer gets a one-day PLAYS_FOR edge with arrangement substitute and a note.
5. Story in lore on the event: Summary, Key moments, Notes in the owner's words; the AI's additions in Agent note. A player of the game is WON from the person to the event.
6. Update the derived season lines in the same breath (rule/stats): the team's standings line and each player's season line (source derived, games_played, as_of, a Derived from chunk). Streak, last-10, home/away and division/conference splits come from the COMPETED_IN edges.
7. Say what changed in one short paragraph: the result, the team's record and streak, the owner's own line if they played, and anything that moved on the leaderboard the owner follows.

lore.title: Averages people will actually quote
lore.content: Points per game, rebounds and assists per game, field goal, three-point and free-throw percentage, effective field goal and true shooting percentage, assist-to-turnover ratio, plus-minus per game, double-doubles. All derived from stored totals over the games that have the component, never stored on a line the AI built. Lead with the coverage: "18.4 a game over the 11 games with a book" and, for percentages, the attempts ("44% on 9.1 attempts"). Qualifying minimum for leaders: the owner's House rules, default 70% of the team's games played. For a rec league with book-points, offer only scoring averages and say the rest is not on file. When comparing the owner's own line with a published one (a league site, a fantasy platform), say which is which and do not overwrite an official or owner line with a derived one.

lore.title: Between games
lore.content:
Next game: get_timeline for the team with event_type match from today, say opponent, date, time, court, and the head-to-head this season from the COMPETED_IN edges. Availability: who is unavailable, doubtful or suspended on the roster edges, with no reasons, and a reminder of the roster minimum if the league has one. Roster news: trades, signings, two-way conversions and affiliate assignments as roster_move events that update roster_list, role and availability per rule/sport_basketball Roster rules and rule/rosters_and_staff. Standings: rebuild stale season lines from the edges (rule/seasons_and_standings), give the team's place in its conference or division with the tiebreaker that decided any tie, and say when the table is partial because the owner only logs their own team. Playoff picture: seeds 1-6 straight in, 7-10 to the play-in, in a 30-team pro league; rec seeding per House rules.
Loading a schedule: one scheduled event per game, status scheduled, confirm-before-bulk, update dates in place when the league moves a game; never create a second event for a moved fixture.

properties.trigger: a fantasy basketball lineup for tonight or this week; setting PG/SG/G/SF/PF/F/C/UTIL/BN/IL slots; a nine-category or points matchup result; rotisserie standings; games left on the bench; a fantasy basketball platform import

data.short_description: The sport-specific weekly routine for a fantasy basketball manager: daily lineup changes and eligibility, closing a points or categories matchup, weekly player lines with games counted, rotisserie standings. Rides on the shared rule/app_fantasy.

lore.title: What this covers
lore.content: The basketball-specific week for a fantasy manager, on top of the shared rule/app_fantasy (which owns rosters, waivers, trades, matchup events and standings mechanics). Read rule/sport_basketball, chunk Fantasy, for slots, categories and the default scoring; read the fantasy competition's House rules for the league's own format, scoring table, roster size and move limits. Tags: basketball, fantasy-basketball, the fantasy season tag.

lore.title: Daily lineups
lore.content:
When the manager sets a lineup ("start Lee at PG tonight, Sam to UTIL, bench the rookie"): update slot on the fantasy PLAYS_FOR edges, check eligibility against each player's real position or secondary_positions (G-F covers SG, SF, G, F; UTIL takes anyone), check the active count against the House rules lineup, warn about a player whose real team has no game today only if the real schedule is on file, and confirm in one line. Slot is the lineup right now and is overwritten; the pack does not keep a per-day history unless the manager asks, in which case append one line per day to a lore chunk on the week's matchup titled Daily lineups ("Tue: PG Lee, SG ..., BN ...").
Weekly-lineup leagues (the lineup locks for the whole scoring period): set slot once, and the matchup PLAYED_IN edges carry that slot.
IL is a slot, not a status: moving a player to IL is slot IL; eligibility is the platform's business; the reason is never stored; the real-team availability changes only if the manager tracks the real league.

lore.title: Closing the week
lore.content:
When the scoring period ends: 1. the matchup event (created by rule/app_fantasy, round "Week N") gets its result: H2H points → home_score/away_score are fantasy points; H2H categories → categories won as the scores, score_display "6-3-0", result tie when categories split evenly; most-categories → 1/0. 2. One PLAYED_IN per rostered player on the matchup (for_team the fantasy team, started true if active on any game day, played true if any game counted). 3. Each player's weekly fantasy line (scope match, RECORDED_IN the matchup, source import): fantasy_points, projected_points, games_counted, games_scheduled, plus the real keys the platform reports (pts, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov, fgm, fga, ftm, fta, fg3m) with the pack's spelling. 4. In categories leagues, the team's week totals as a round-scope team stat_line RECORDED_IN the matchup (fgm, fga, fg_pct, ftm, fta, ft_pct, fg3m, pts, reb, ast, stl, blk, tov, categories_won/lost/tied), the platform's rounding as given. 5. Update the fantasy team's season line (wins, losses, ties; roto leagues: the category totals and roto_points). 6. Tell the manager the result, the categories that swung it, and the games left on the bench (games_scheduled - games_counted across the active roster) if the data is there.
Rotisserie leagues have no matchups: step 4 goes on the season line directly and standings are the roto grid: rank each category across the league's season lines, N points for first down to 1, ties split, sum, and say the as_of date.
Real stats and fantasy stats disagree sometimes (stat corrections, platform rounding): the real game line is what happened, the fantasy line is what scored; show both, labelled, when asked.
